The trip was a RydeX fixed-quote booking: $23.18 total made up of base $3.90, distance $13.88 (9.84 km), time $3.93 (15.1 min), waiting $0.00 and platform $1.47 [F6], with billed distance exactly the optimal 9.8 km [F4] and no surge [F5]. Under RD-2 the non-metered branch applies, so extra kilometres driven do not enter the fare and there is no refundable distance component [F4][F6][RD-2]. FARE-1 is also satisfied because every item charged is a published component (base, distance, time, platform) with no ERP/toll or post-trip unpublished add-on, so nothing is refundable there either [F6][FARE-1].

One off-route segment is measured, 10:04–10:11, 3.98 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.77 km, adding 2.21 km and reaching up to 1039 m off route — far beyond the 0.2 km data-layer noise tolerance, so RD-1 is engaged on it [F3][RD-1]. RD-4 cannot exempt it: no traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window [F14], and while Tampines Expressway is at speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) only for 09:48–10:04 [F11], I read RD-4(b) as corroboration directed at the substituted stretch (up to the 10:04 turn-off), not as a standalone exemption, and the trace also fails RD-4(a) [F11][F14][RD-4].

The rider's consent is genuine but its scope is not settled on this record. Before the segment began, the driver asked at 10:01 "Jam on Tampines Expressway is building up ahead, can I go round via Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1?" [F7] and the rider answered at 10:01 "Sure, no problem." [F8] — a rider message sent before the 10:04 start, so RD-5's "before you go" timing test is met, with a complete, fully timestamped chat record (2 messages) so there is no G12 completeness gap [F8][F9][RD-5]. The words name one specific road, so this is a specific named-road authorisation under RD-5: it covers driving on Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1 only, and the record must tie the segment to that road [F7][F8][RD-5]. Nothing does: the fact table carries no road name for the driven path, and the driver's post-trip statement naming the same road is a claim, not consent [F3][F10][RD-5]. Nothing places the segment elsewhere either — no stop, no location message, no alternative road. The finding on F3 is therefore undetermined (G13), which is permitted here: on a fixed fare this changes no amount and no account mark, so the case can still be ruled [F4][F6][RD-2].

The driver's statement that the rider agreed verbally [F10] adds nothing to the exemption analysis, since a driver's assertion of agreement is not rider consent [F10][RD-5]. RD-6 does not apply: the driver has 0 disputes and 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days [F17], so there is no "repeated" breach and no flag_account [F17][RD-6]. RD-3 is not in play — no stop was requested or measured; the rider's message named no place to stop [F7][F8][RD-3]. The refundable amount on the non-metered branch is zero (no detour-linked add-on in F6 [F6][F4]), and RD-2 directs no_action where the refundable amount is 0, while still recording the RD-1 shortest-route breach [F3][RD-2]. A refund cannot be computed from a gps or fare distance rate here because RydeX is a fixed quote, so amount is null.

Safety screen: I read the driver's request and the rider's reply [F7][F8], the driver's post-trip statement [F10] and the complaint — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears; this is a route-and-fare argument only, so no SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation [F7][F8][F10][SAFE-1]. Evidence is sufficient: the segment is measured [F3], the fare breakdown and billed distance are complete [F4][F6], the consent chat is complete and timestamped [F9], and the traffic record settles RD-4 [F11][F14].

? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F3] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 10:04:50 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes no amount (fixed fare) and no flag: if you cannot settle it, undetermined is allowed and the case may still be ruled. ? RD-3 rider-requested stop; whether the rider named this place [F3] RULE (RD-3(a)): exempt if a RIDER message before the segment named a specific place and the car stopped there (the whole way there is exempt; how long the stop lasted or how far the place was does not reduce it). A stop the rider asked for without naming a place ('a 7-Eleven on the way') does not excuse the driver's choice of a far one → counts. No stop measured in this segment. (F7, F8)

claims.assertion: The GPS track shows one off-route segment, 10:04–10:11, where 3.98 km were driven over ground the optimal route covers in 1.77 km, adding 2.21 km and reaching up to 1039 m from the optimal route; this is an off-route segment under RD-1 and is not matched-noise (0.2 km tolerance).

The driver did ask before the turn-off and the rider replied 'Sure, no problem.' at 10:01 (Chat #2), one minute after the driver's request named Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1 and three minutes before the segment started at 10:04, so the message is pre-segment rider consent under RD-5.

That consent is only a general authorisation to avoid the jam ('can I go round via ... ?' — the rider agreed to a reroute, not to a named road), and no fact ties the driven segment to Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1 itself, so per RD-5 the scope of the consent as it relates to the actual road driven is undetermined; the segment is not automatically exempted.

The driver's post-trip statement that the rider agreed (F10) is a driver statement, not consent; consent can only come from the rider's own pre-segment message (F8), so F10 adds nothing to the exemption analysis.

The driver's congestion justification is only partially corroborated: Tampines Expressway was band 2 (10–19 km/h) during 09:48–10:04, which supports congestion on the optimal route at the moment of the turn-off, but there is no traffic incident anywhere near the route (F14), so RD-4(a) cannot exempt the segment and RD-4(c) applies.

The price-affected harm is nil: this was a RydeX fixed-quote trip charged $23.18 with billed distance 9.8 km, exactly the optimal distance, no surge, and $0.00 waiting fee — the extra 2.6 km actually driven did not change the fare.

Because this is a non-metered service where the fare is a one-off quote unaffected by mileage, and no unexempted-segment ERP/toll or post-trip unpublished add-on appears in the breakdown ($3.90 base + $13.88 distance + $3.93 time + $1.47 platform), the refundable amount under RD-2 is 0 and the correct disposition on money is no_action — with the RD-1 shortest-route breach recorded.

The rider accepts only that the fare is not reduced, not that the 2.21 km detour was justified: the 21.8-minute trip ran 6.7 minutes longer than the 15.1-minute estimate, a genuine service-quality loss to the rider even though the fixed quote did not move.

Both parties are clean in the 90-day window (rider 0 disputes/0 upheld; driver 0 disputes/0 upheld over 960 trips), so RD-6's repeated-route-dispute condition is not met and no flag_account is requested here.
Nothing in the chat, the complaint or the driver's statement is a threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation is not triggered by this record.

(F8) at 10:01 is genuine pre-segment consent under RD-5, so the driver will argue the whole segment is exempt; my counter is only that the scope is a general reroute authority with no record tying the drive to Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1 (F7, F3), which the judge may resolve as undetermined rather than as a breach.

Traffic band 2 on Tampines Expressway during 09:48–10:04 (F11) directly corroborates the driver's stated reason for the reroute on the very segment being replaced, so the driver will lean on RD-4(a)/(b); my answer is that RD-4 requires a traffic-incident fact and F14 records none, but a judge may still read the congestion as a reasonable cause under RD-4.

My own modelling concedes zero monetary harm — F4 shows the billed distance equals the optimal distance and F6 shows a fixed $23.18 with no detour-linked add-ons — so the RD-2 outcome may legitimately be no_action (F5).

claims.assertion: This is a RydeX fixed-quote trip: the fare was quoted up front at 9.84 km / 15.1 min and the meter did not run, so no additional distance was billed to the rider (F4, F6).

The only off-route segment is 10:04–10:11, which added 2.21 km over the optimal route's 1.77 km for that stretch (F3), so any exposure is limited to that single segment, not to the 2.6 km overall trip difference (F1).

Before leaving the optimal route the driver asked the rider in-app at 10:01: 'Jam on Tampines Expressway is building up ahead, can I go round via Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1?' (F7), and the rider replied in the same chat at 10:01: 'Sure, no problem.' (F8).
The rider's consent message (F8, 10:01) is timestamped before the off-route segment began at 10:04 (F3), so it satisfies RD-5's 'before you go' requirement on timing.

The consent is a specific named-road authorisation — the rider agreed to 'round via Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1' (F7/F8) — and the whole off-route segment (F3) is the single continuous run that the agreed diversion produced; there is no record of any stop, location message or named road placing the car anywhere else, so the segment should be read as the agreed Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1 detour rather than an undetermined deviation.

The driver's reason for the diversion was congestion on the expressway, and the traffic record corroborates it: TAMPINES EXPRESSWAY was at speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) during 09:48–10:04 (F11), i.e. the expressway section immediately before the 10:04 turn-off (F3).

RD-4(b) treats such a band 1–2 record on a road of the substituted optimal route as corroboration of a justified reroute; no traffic incident was recorded (F14), but the band 2 reading covering the turn-off time corroborates the driver's stated ground rather than contradicting it.

Because the service is a non-metered RydeX fixed quote, RD-2's non-metered branch is the one that applies, and the rider's own complaint that 'the fare was a fixed quote' concedes the fare could not have been inflated by the extra distance (F4, F6).

No ERP/toll or post-trip manual add-on was charged that could be refunded under the non-metered branch: the total of $23.18 comprises only base $3.90, distance $13.88, time $3.93, waiting $0.00 and platform $1.47 (F6), so the refundable amount on the deviation is zero.

No account flag is warranted: the driver has 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days (F17), so RD-6's 'repeated' precondition is absent and this case cannot make the record repeated (F17).
The chat record is complete — 2 messages, every one timestamped (F9) — so there is no G12-style evidentiary gap that would force the case to a human reviewer on the consent question.
Nothing in the chat (F7, F8, F10) or in the rider's complaint reads as a threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation is not triggered.

weaknesses: The GPS record does not name any road, so nothing ties the driven segment (F3) to 'Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1': there is no stop, no location message and no road-name fact for that stretch. The rider will argue that under the specific-route limb of RD-5 (and G13) the judge must find the segment 'undetermined' rather than consented.

The consent in F8 — 'Sure, no problem.' — is a bare two-word reply. The rider will argue it is at most a general 'go whichever is faster' authorisation, which under RD-5 does not cover a segment that runs up to 1039 m off the optimal route (F3).

RD-4(b) is not a standalone exemption for a band 2 reading: F11 only shows congestion on TAMPINES EXPRESSWAY at band 2 during 09:48–10:04 and F14 records no incident at all, so the rider will say the reroute rests on corroboration only and cannot by itself exempt the segment under RD-4(a).

The hard numbers look bad on their face and the rider will lead with them: 12.4 km actual vs 9.8 km optimal, +2.6 km / +26% (F1), and 21.8 min vs 15.1 min estimated (F2), plus the driver's own post-trip statement (F10) asserting a consent the rider may say is better explained as mere politeness.

Accepted that only the 10:04–10:11 segment is in issue — F3 gives 3.98 km driven vs 1.77 km optimal, +2.21 km, up to 1039 m off the optimal route — and that segment alone exceeds the data-layer noise tolerance, so RD-1 is engaged on it.
